sheets.note: Drill instruction: Take any verse and circle it with questions before moving on — τίς; τί ἐποίησεν; ποῦ; πότε; διὰ τί; The information is not the point; the repetition is.

terms.english: Who? Which one? (gen. τίνος, dat. τίνι, acc. τίνα)

examples.greek: τίς ἄρα οὗτός ἐστιν ὅτι καὶ ὁ ἄνεμος καὶ ἡ θάλασσα ὑπακούει αὐτῷ;
examples.english: Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?

examples.greek: ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνα με λέγετε εἶναι;
examples.english: But you — who do you say that I am?
Where did this man get these things?

examples.greek: πόθεν τούτους δυνήσεταί τις ὧδε χορτάσαι ἄρτων ἐπ' ἐρημίας;
examples.english: From where will anyone be able to feed these people with bread here in the wilderness?
What do you want me to do for you?

examples.greek: τί δειλοί ἐστε; οὔπω ἔχετε πίστιν;
examples.english: Why are you afraid? Have you still no faith?

examples.greek: καὶ πῶς πάσας τὰς παραβολὰς γνώσεσθε;
examples.english: Then how will you understand all the parables?

examples.greek: πῶς λέγουσιν οἱ γραμματεῖς ὅτι ὁ χριστὸς υἱὸς Δαυίδ ἐστιν;
examples.english: How do the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?

examples.greek: ποῦ ἐστιν τὸ κατάλυμά μου ὅπου τὸ πάσχα μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν μου φάγω;
examples.english: Where is my guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?

examples.greek: ποῦ θέλεις ἀπελθόντες ἑτοιμάσωμεν ἵνα φάγῃς τὸ πάσχα;
examples.english: Where do you want us to go and prepare for you to eat the Passover?
Tell us, when will these things be?

examples.greek: οὐκ οἴδατε γὰρ πότε ὁ καιρός ἐστιν.
examples.english: For you do not know when the time is.

examples.greek: διὰ τί οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ τῶν Φαρισαίων νηστεύουσιν, οἱ δὲ σοὶ μαθηταὶ οὐ νηστεύουσιν;
examples.english: Why do John's disciples and the Pharisees' disciples fast, but your disciples do not fast?
Why did you not believe him?

sheets.note: Drill instruction: Take any verse and circle it with questions before moving on — τίς; τί ἐποίησεν; ποῦ; πότε; διὰ τί; The information is not the point; the repetition is.

examples.english: By what authority are you doing these things?
Which commandment is first of all?
How many loaves do you have? Go and see.
How many loaves do you have?

examples.greek: πόσος χρόνος ἐστὶν ὡς τοῦτο γέγονεν αὐτῷ;
examples.english: How long has it been since this happened to him?

examples.greek: ποσάκις ἁμαρτήσει εἰς ἐμὲ ὁ ἀδελφός μου καὶ ἀφήσω αὐτῷ;
examples.english: How often shall my brother sin against me and I forgive him?

examples.greek: ποσάκις ἠθέλησα ἐπισυναγαγεῖν τὰ τέκνα σου.
examples.english: How often I longed to gather your children together.

examples.greek: ἴδετε πηλίκοις ὑμῖν γράμμασιν ἔγραψα τῇ ἐμῇ χειρί.
examples.english: See with what large letters I have written to you with my own hand.
See how great this man was.

examples.greek: διδάσκαλε, ἴδε ποταποὶ λίθοι καὶ ποταπαὶ οἰκοδομαί.
examples.english: Teacher, look — what stones and what buildings!

examples.greek: διελογίζετο ποταπὸς εἴη ὁ ἀσπασμὸς οὗτος.
examples.english: She wondered what sort of greeting this might be.

examples.greek: τί ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον, εἰπεῖν … ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι, ἢ εἰπεῖν· ἔγειρε;
examples.english: Which is easier, to say 'your sins are forgiven', or to say 'Rise'?

sheets.description: The first layer of fluency is social, not grammatical. Say these before you understand them — they are the phrases that let you stay in a Greek-only room without switching back.

terms.english: Thank you (lit. I give thanks to you)
I am glad you are well
By no means, not at all
Say it to me in Greek

principles.title: χαῖρε as imperative
principles.explanation: χαῖρε is an imperative — literally 'rejoice!' Greek greeting is a command to be glad. The reply is simply χαῖρε καὶ σύ.

sheets.drill_instruction: Practice greetings in context: meeting someone, parting, asking how they are, responding to questions about origins and names. All interaction must stay in Greek — use language phrases to ask for clarification rather than switching to English.

sheets.description: Essential classroom language for asking permission, requesting repetition, checking understanding, and managing comprehension in Greek-only environments.

examples.english: Is it permitted or not permitted?

terms.english: I want to ask you something.

examples.english: they said the same thing to him
he cried out with a loud voice
Do you understand all these things?

terms.english: What part of speech is it?

examples.english: he said, I do not know
they had forgotten to bring bread
Let us go to the next towns

terms.english: It is finished / that's the end.

examples.english: they have come to an end

principles: The subjunctive mood (ἄγωμεν, ἀρξώμεθα) expresses cohortative wishes: 'let us...'
τί vs ποῖος: τί (what?) for identity or substance; ποῖος (what kind?) for quality or category
In Greek-only instruction, these phrases keep learners engaged without resorting to English metalanguage
sheets.drill_instruction: Circle-and-Ask Drill: Take any verse and circle out with questions: τίς; τί ἐποίησεν; ποῦ; πότε; διὰ τί; The information is secondary; the repetition builds neural pathways. Start with simple narratives (Mark's healing stories) where concrete objects invite questions.

sheets.description: Imperative commands for classroom management paired with vocabulary for people, writing materials, furniture, and spatial relationships in the learning environment.

examples.english: Listen to the voice of the Lord
there was a certain female disciple
in the book of the law
at the door of the school

principles: Imperative mood distinguishes by number and voice: ἄκουε (sg.) vs ἀκούετε (pl.); ἔγειρε (active) vs ἀνάστηθι (middle/deponent)
Total Physical Response (TPR) drills use commands without translation: the body demonstrates understanding before the mind explains it
Spatial prepositions with the genitive (ἐπὶ τῆς τραπέζης), dative (παρὰ τῇ θύρᾳ), and accusative (ὑπὸ τὴν κλίνην) encode different meanings
sheets.drill_instruction: Total-Physical-Response (TPR) Drill: The teacher commands; the class obeys in silence. Example sequence: ἔγειρε· ἐλθὲ πρὸς τὴν θύραν· ἄνοιξον τὴν θύραν· κάθισον. No translation, no explanation. Comprehension shows up in the body first, then language follows.

sheets.description: Essential vocabulary for expressing hunger, thirst, food requests, eating preferences, and dining actions in everyday conversation.

examples.english: I am thirsty and have nothing to drink

terms.english: I am not hungry any more.
I do not want to eat.
It is good; it is delicious.
I am going off to eat.

principles: δός (aorist imperative) asks for the thing once, one specific request — pass me the bread. δίδου (present imperative) asks for it habitually — keep giving me bread. Mark's aorist imperatives are almost always the single, decisive request.
The middle voice of ἐσθίω (φάγομαι) emphasizes personal participation in eating; the active voice emphasizes the action itself
Dining customs in Mark: reclined at table, bread broken and shared, wine passed around
sheets.drill_instruction: Substitution Drill: Start with 'δός μοι τὸν ἄρτον' and substitute: δός μοι τὸ ποτήριον, δός μοι τὸ ἅλας, δός μοι τὸ κρέας. This builds muscle memory for the accusative object constructions.

examples.english: for every one shall be salted with fire

principles: Neuter nouns: ἔλαιον, ὕδωρ, γάλα, κρέας, ᾠόν, ποτήριον, πῦρ
Masculine nouns: ἄρτος, σῖτος, κόκκος, οἶνος, ἰχθύς, πίναξ, κλίβανος, ξέστης
Feminine nouns: τράπεζα, ζύμη, ὑδρία, σπυρίς, συκῆ, σταφυλή
sheets.drill_instruction: Substitution Drill: Teacher names a food or vessel item, students respond with accusative constructions. Example: Teacher says 'ἄρτος', students say 'δός μοι τὸν ἄρτον', 'φέρε τὸν ἄρτον', 'ἐσθίε τὸν ἄρτον', etc.

examples.english: I am drowsy from the fire
they will rest from their toils
I am going into the bedroom

principles: Neuter nouns: ἱμάτιον, τὸ ταμεῖον, ἀνάγαιον
Masculine: χιτών, κραβάττος, κοιτών
Feminine: κλίνη, χλαῖνα, σινδών, ζώνη, στρωμνή
Imperative forms: ἔγειρε! ἀνάστηθι! γρηγόρει! κοιμηθῶμεν
sheets.drill_instruction: Substitution Drill: Teacher gives imperative commands for sleep/waking actions. Example: Teacher says 'κοιμᾶσθε' (you sleep), students respond 'κοιμηθῶμεν ἤδη' (let us sleep now), 'ἀνάστηθι' (rise), etc. Builds imperative fluency for rest routines.

examples.english: the upper storey of the city

principles: Feminine: νύξ, σελήνη, λυχνία, θύρα, αὐλή, οἰκία
Neuter: σκότος, ταμεῖον, ἀνάγαιον, ὑπερῷον, δῶμα, ἐνύπνιον, ὄναρ
Masculine: ἀλέκτωρ, λύχνος, ὄρθρος, οἶκος, ὕπνος
Genitive of time: νυκτός (by night), πρωΐ (in early morning)
sheets.drill_instruction: Substitution Drill: Teacher provides time expressions, students respond with nocturnal activities. Example: Teacher says 'μεσονύκτιον', students say 'μεσονύκτιον καθεύδουσιν', 'μεσονύκτιον ἀναπαύονται', etc. Builds vocabulary for understanding Mark's night scenes and dream narratives.
